name: throttled-py-bounded-resilient-store-operations
instr:
Give store callers one bounded, cancellable, retry-aware operation policy across synchronous and asynchronous memory and Redis stores. Controlled calls retain established command results while exposing durable outcome accounting, and uncontrolled calls remain fully compatible.

A StoreOperation applies one absolute monotonic budget across lock waits, lazy connections, backend execution, and retry delays, and rejects nonpositive max_attempts before backend work begins. Reports count started and completed attempts monotonically, freeze with one terminal reason, and make a completed operation single use. StoreOperationFailure distinguishes cancellation, deadline expiry, and retry exhaustion, carries the final report and last backend exception, and chains that exception as its cause. Reads retry only StoreUnavailableError transport failures; mutations do so only with retry_mutations=True, while validation and cancellation never retry. Memory lock failure leaves values, recency, eviction, and locks untouched, while async task or operation cancellation releases any acquired lock exactly once. Sync and async Redis operations use matching accounting, stop cancellation before another attempt, and preserve conversion and lazy-connection behavior. Calls without operation control preserve existing values, errors, validation timing, and StoreUnavailableError translation. The remaining synchronous declarations are `exists(self, key, *, operation=None)`, `ttl(self, key, *, operation=None)`,
